body.en: In BCD (8421 code) each decimal digit is written as its own 4-bit binary group; codes 1010 to 1111 are invalid. BCD is a weighted code (weights 8, 4, 2, 1). Excess-3 is obtained by adding 3 (0011) to each BCD digit; it is non-weighted and self-complementing (the 1's complement of a digit's code gives the code of its 9's complement).

narration.en: In B C D each decimal digit gets its own four bits. Excess-three adds three to each digit before coding.
narration.kn: ಬಿಸಿಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ದಶಮಾಂಶ ಅಂಕಿಗೆ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಬಿಟ್‌ಗಳು. ಎಕ್ಸೆಸ್-3 ಪ್ರತಿ ಅಂಕಿಗೆ ಮೂರು ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಸಂಕೇತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: BCD, Excess-3 and Gray

say.en: In BCD each decimal digit gets its own 4 bits. 47 becomes 0100 for the 4 and 0111 for the 7.
Excess-3: add 3, that is 0011, to each BCD digit. 4 becomes 0111 and 7 becomes 1010.
Gray code: copy the MSB, then each Gray bit is the XOR of two neighbouring binary bits. 1101 becomes 1011.
ASCII is a 7-bit code for letters, digits and symbols. Capital A is 65, which is 1000001.

narration.en: BCD writes each decimal digit as its own 4 bits; Excess-3 adds 3 to each digit; straight binary converts the whole number; Gray code changes only one bit between neighbouring numbers. Step through the numbers and compare the rows.
narration.kn: BCD ಪ್ರತಿ ದಶಮಾಂಶ ಅಂಕಿಯನ್ನು 4 ಬಿಟ್‌ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬರೆಯುತ್ತದೆ; ಎಕ್ಸೆಸ್-3 ಪ್ರತಿ ಅಂಕಿಗೆ 3 ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಗ್ರೇ ಕೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಪಕ್ಕದ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ಒಂದೇ ಬಿಟ್ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: In Gray code only one bit changes between successive numbers, so it avoids errors in shaft encoders. Binary → Gray: the MSB is copied, then each Gray bit is the XOR of adjacent binary bits. Gray → binary: copy the MSB, then each binary bit is the XOR of the previous binary bit and the next Gray bit. ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange) is a 7-bit alphanumeric code; for example 'A' = 65 = 1000001.

points.en: Gray: one-bit change between successive values (unit-distance)

narration.en: Gray code changes only one bit at a time, which is why it is used in position encoders. ASCII gives every letter and symbol a seven-bit code.

narration.en: Recap. BCD codes each decimal digit in 4 bits. Excess-3 = BCD + 3; self-complementing. Gray code: only one bit changes at a time. ASCII is a 7-bit alphanumeric code.
